work: Rules On Hurrying To Mourning Rites
heading: Liji 31 · Ben Sang 奔喪 · Rules On Hurrying To Mourning Rites · Ben Sang 1 … Ben Sang 12

items.text: When you hear of a relative's death, wail with full grief and set out immediately for the mourning rites.
items.quote: he wailed as he answered the messenger, and gave full vent to his sorrow.

items.text: If the rites are for your father or mother, travel night and day until you arrive.
items.quote: Only when the rites were those for a father or a mother did he travel while he could yet see the stars, and rested when he (again) saw them.

items.text: As presiding mourner, wail before the coffin, bare your arms, and leap.
items.quote: He knelt on the east of the coffin, with his face to the west, and wailed, giving full vent to his grief.

items.text: Receive mourning visitors with bows and leaping, and escort them to the gate.
items.quote: He bowed to the visitors, leaping with them, and escorted them (to the gate), returning (afterwards) to his place.

items.text: As a wife, join the mourning for your parents-in-law: wail, wear the lower cincture, and leap alternately with the presiding mourner.
items.quote: When a wife hurried to the mourning rites, she went up to the hall by the (side) steps on the east

items.text: If you arrive after the burial, go first to the grave, kneel and wail, then return to the house for mourning.
items.quote: he first went to the grave; and there kneeling with his face to the north, he wailed, giving full vent to his sorrow.

items.text: Family members keep the morning and evening wailing places throughout the mourning.
items.quote: The husbands and wives (of the family) waited for him at the wailing-places for every morning and evening

items.text: Wail for your elder brother's wife (your sister-in-law) even though you do not wear mourning for her.
items.quote: a place was chosen in which to wail for one for whom mourning was not worn, was the death of a sister-in-law, the wife of an elder brother.

items.text: Wear a hempen sash for a married female relative who has died, even though you do not wear full mourning for her.
items.quote: For a female member of the family who had married, and for whom therefore mourning was not worn, the hempen sash was assumed.

items.text: When a great officer comes to condole, bare your arms and bow to him.
items.quote: a Great officer came (to condole with him), he bared his arms, and bowed to him.

items.text: When an ordinary officer comes to condole, cover your arms and then bow to him.
items.quote: In the case of a similar visit from an ordinary officer, he covered his arms, and then bowed to him.

work: Rules On Hurrying To Mourning Rites
heading: Liji 31 · Ben Sang 奔喪 · Rules On Hurrying To Mourning Rites · Ben Sang 13 … Ben Sang 29

items.text: When hurrying to mourning rites for a parent, begin wailing as soon as you see the home district.
items.quote: One hurrying to mourning rites, if they were for a parent, wailed when he looked towards the district

items.text: When hurrying to mourning rites for other relations, wail at the gate, door, or station according to the closeness of the relation.
items.quote: if for a relation for whom nine months' mourning was due, he wailed when he could see the gate of his house

items.text: If you cannot attend the mourning rites, make a place where you are and wail, baring your arms and leaping to show grief.
items.quote: When one heard of the mourning rites, and it was impossible to hurry to be present, he wailed and gave full vent to his grief.

items.text: If you return after the mourning rites are completed, go to the grave and wail before putting off your mourning.
items.quote: If one returned home after the mourning rites had been completed, he went to the grave, and there wailed and went through the leaping

items.text: Wail for relatives and non-relatives in the place prescribed for each degree of relationship: the ancestral temple for a father's relation, the back chamber for a mother's or wife's relative, outside the gate for a teacher, outside the door for a friend, and in the open country for an acquaintance.
items.quote: For one of his father's relations, a man wailed in the ancestral temple; for one of his mother or wife's relatives, in the back chamber
items.conflict: Wailing in an ancestral temple may involve honoring ancestors; Christians should avoid idolatrous worship places.

items.text: As father, preside over the mourning rites of the household if you are alive.
items.quote: At all mourning rites in a household, if the father were alive, he acted as presiding mourner.

items.text: When the father is dead, the eldest among equally related brothers, or the nearest relation, presides over the mourning rites.
items.quote: If two brothers were equally related to the deceased, the eldest presided at those rites; if they were not equally related, the one most nearly so presided.

items.text: If you hear of a brother's death after the mourning period would have ended, still put on mourning and perform the leaping.
items.quote: When one heard of the death of a brother at a distance, but the news did not arrive till the time which his own mourning would have taken had expired, he put on the mourning cincture and went through the leaping.

items.text: As presiding mourner, bow to visitors who come to condole and escort them out.
items.quote: When the visitors went out, the presiding mourner bowed to them and escorted them.
